knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The procedure says to read the manufacturer's dilution instructions, assess ventilation and use the PPE specified for the product and task. Before dilution, check those instructions together with ventilation, splash risk and the people nearby. Colour and smell do not show strength, and a stronger mix is not a check.
The worked scenario rejects a doubled concentrate and redirects to the approved dilution and mechanical cleaning. A stronger mix is not automatically more effective.
The lesson says to read the manufacturer's dilution instructions, use a dedicated labelled measuring system, and never estimate concentration by colour or smell.

practicalCriteria: Measures accurately, labels appropriately and selects controls for splash and inhalation exposure.
Explains applicable scope and site procedures
Demonstrates hazard controls and safe stop-work decisions
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 2: Read the manufacturer's dilution instructions on the product label and measure using a dedicated, labelled measuring system; this lesson gives no dilution ratios.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 3 is not done: Never estimate concentration by colour or smell, and do not strengthen a mix on the view that it will work better.
Stop work if procedure step 7 is not done: If the surface, the soil or hazard, or the approved method is unclear, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance.
